terms.definition: A sort where two elements with equal keys keep their original relative order.
terms.example: Sorting [ (B,2), (A,1), (B,1) ] by number gives [ (A,1), (B,1), (B,2) ] — the two B's keep their original order relative to each other.

terms.definition: A strategy that splits a problem into smaller sub-problems, solves each recursively, then combines the results.
terms.example: Merge sort splits an array in half, sorts each half recursively, then merges the two sorted halves.

terms.definition: Extra, temporary storage used during an algorithm, separate from the input array.
terms.example: Merge sort's merge step copies elements into a temporary array before writing the merged result back.
